Why is the sky blue, but sunsets red?
Why is the sky blue, but sunsets red?
Same sun,
same air.
Only the path through
the air changes.
Sunlight is every colour
mixed together.
Air molecules knock some
of it sideways,
and they scatter blue
about six times more
strongly than red.
That scattered blue
reaches you from every
direction.
That's the blue sky.
At sunset,
the light skims in
almost flat,
through about 38 times more air.
Even in clean air,
less than a thousandth
of the blue survives
that trip.
About a quarter of the red does.
So the sun glows orange and red.
And the blue you lost?
Somebody to the west
gets it,
as their afternoon sky.
